BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of the Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** The Seller documents are the counterparty's draft. I reviewed them against our playbook and did not treat them as instructions.

**Overall view:** The Seller's package moves liability, disclosure, conditions and completion mechanics substantially in its favour. Several positions go below our fallbacks, and Amelia Frost has not authorised any fallback. One position (no fraud carve-out) is outside our authority to concede at all. **We should reject the package as drafted and respond on our starting positions.**

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price, AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25%, AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject and counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure is our conditional fallback, and Amelia Frost has given no written authority for this draft, so we cannot accept it.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess above the basket recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once it is exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** The Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and the deductible structure permanently removes AUD 250,000 of recoverable loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. It also proposes that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months, with the time limit confined to general Warranty Claims.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject and counter at 24 months.** Delete the "applies to all Claims" default. 18 months is an unapproved fallback, and the default would quietly extend short time limits to fundamental, tax, fraud and indemnity claims.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties would sit under the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with:
  - a 100% cap;
  - a claims period of at least six years; and
  - no general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Title and capacity are the core of what we are buying, and capping them at 20% for 18 months is not an administrative matter.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5). There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. This is non-negotiable.** The playbook says no one may waive this carve-out, so it is not open to trade at any level.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, the Accounts, the statutory registers and publicly searchable records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties only.
- **Recommendation:** **Strike DL 1.1 and 1.2.** Keep only the specific disclosures in sections 2–10, tested for fairness. Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure would gut the warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the clause. If any qualifier survives, it should:
  - turn on named Seller knowledge persons making reasonable enquiry; and
  - never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3.** It is a blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion that would defeat the specific indemnities for matters we have already identified (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses).

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only, with the condition treated as satisfied once Bluefen's written consent is delivered. DL section 2 confirms there is no final consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** A Completion condition requiring an effective consent plus evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions have been satisfied.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the reasonable-endeavours and consent-on-delivery wording.** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (about AUD 3,600,000), and a consent with unmet conditions may not be effective.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release to be provided after Completion. About AUD 3,200,000 is outstanding, and DL section 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge has been provided.
- **Buyer wants:** At or before Completion:
  - a current payout letter;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds; and
  - effective security releases (the clause 8.1 change-control and clause 9.2 discharge mechanics in DD-003).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** A post-completion release would leave us owning a company with live security and change-of-control exposure. That approach is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, and neither exists.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. DL section 5 confirms they are absent and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** The bonuses plus any triggered on-costs either shown as a specific funds-flow line item (as a Debt-type deduction or paid from Seller proceeds) or otherwise expressly Seller-funded. This should be backed by an indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the silent exclusion.** These are Completion-triggered liabilities of the Company, and leaving them out of the funds flow shifts them to us.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity, limited to the SOW3 payment, is "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering:
  - loss from any failure of the SOW3 Project Materials to transfer;
  - third-party IP claims; and
  - remediation.

  We should preserve the cure under DD-004 clause 7.3, ideally through evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees plus a confirmatory assignment before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Broaden the indemnity.** The risk is title to the IP, not just a payment amount. Note that the AUD 180,000 in DD-010 is not independently verified as either paid or unpaid, so it should not be treated as the measure of exposure.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material.
- **Buyer wants:** Covenants to:
  - preserve logs;
  - complete the investigation (scope, whether any access occurred, whether notification is required); and
  - provide regular updates before Completion.

  We should also seek specific protection (an indemnity) for losses arising from the incident.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "not material" characterisation, but do not overstate the matter either.** On the current record there is no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss in either direction. The about 1,240 records and the open questions justify investigation and protection, not a price figure.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Diligence on whether each renewal is:
  - unavoidable or terminable;
  - accrued or prepaid; and
  - genuinely ordinary course, reading DD-008 and DD-011 together.
- **Recommendation:** **Neither accept nor reject yet; assess first.** DL section 8 itself does not answer these questions. Per the playbook, there should be no automatic Debt classification or price deduction until the facts are known.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Limitations apply to all Claims of any nature, and limitations default to all Claims unless stated otherwise (cl 9.3 / 12.3 / 12.8 / 13 / 20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Separate, express regimes for Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants, with general limitations applying only to general Warranty Claims.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the global application language.** It is a hidden override that would collapse every category into the general regime.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register. DL section 10 concedes that this does not mean the Buyer has verified title.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of:
  - title and ownership (for example, an ASIC search reconciled to the register and share issue and transfer history);
  - no encumbrances (for example, a PPSR search plus confirmation of the Riverlark release); and
  - Seller authority (board and shareholder approvals).

  The Title warranties should sit in the fundamental regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept DD-012 as sufficient.** It is an internal, Seller-supplied source, not independent proof.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Both remain open and are negotiated separately. We should assume neither unlimited liability nor any agreed resolution.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation.** Record Tax and IP as open items; nothing has been agreed, and folding them into the general regime would also breach category separation.

---

### Other points from the Disclosure Letter
- **DL 1.4 (no admissions):** We can accept a reasonable form of this clause. It must not, however, be read to qualify the conditions or indemnities.
- **DL 7 (office lease, DD-007) and DL 9 (Mossvale, DD-009):** The materials describe a notification obligation and an assignment restriction, not a consent requirement for a share sale. These are worth confirming in diligence but are not currently consent conditions.
- **Authority:** No playbook fallback (20% cap, 18 months, post-completion Riverlark release) is available unless Amelia Frost gives written approval that identifies this draft. I recommend the mark-up go back on our starting positions.
